title: Seven Deadly Fitness Sins: Gluttony
summary: Closing entry of the Seven Deadly Fitness Sins series: NH frames gluttony as overconsumption of anything, from 10k-calorie challenges and dirty bulks to undereating (negative gluttony) and binge-watching YouTube fitness. The fix is awareness: question why you consume each thing.
claims: Gluttony in fitness is overconsumption of anything, not only food
10k-calorie challenges are gluttony for views: excess calories are purged or just turned into fat
Excess body fat is a direct sign of having overeaten at some point; when he was bulking he ate far too much, wasting food and worsening his health
Treat food as a finite resource and eat only what your body needs; anything above or below means something is off
Undereating is negative gluttony: starving yourself also reflects a lost balance with food
Constantly watching YouTube fitness is information gluttony; at least 40% of the videos you watch do nothing for you or harm your mental health
Fitness media is designed like junk food: consumable and pleasurable even when it lacks value
To fight gluttony, question your consumption: ask why you consume each thing and reject intruders
Nobody slips into a vice by design; it happens through lack of awareness
